methodological_rigor.justification: This is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm phase II interventional study (n = 30) adding one postinduction blinatumomab course to an established chemotherapy backbone, which is appropriate for early efficacy/safety exploration but limits causal inference (Methods; Abstract). Long-term outcomes (DFS/OS) are compared against selected and individually matched historical controls from Interfant-06, which strengthens context but remains vulnerable to residual confounding and era effects (Methods; Figures description). Time-to-event endpoints are clearly defined with censoring rules, and the manuscript references matched-control methodology and supplemental statistical details, but those key analytic specifics are not fully visible in the normalized main text (Methods; References to Data Supplement). Overall, small sample size and reliance on historical comparators are the main methodological constraints despite clinically large observed differences in survival.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is a prospective interventional cohort with historical control comparisons rather than a randomized trial, which maps most closely to Oxford LoE 2b as nondefinitive clinical evidence (Methods; Abstract). Clinical relevance is high because it targets a very high-risk population (infants with KMT2A-rearranged CD19+ B-ALL) and reports durable improvements in 4-year DFS and OS compared with Interfant-06 controls (Abstract; Figures). The inclusion of toxicity/infection outcomes and pharmacokinetic characterization further supports translational relevance for frontline regimen design in this age group (Methods; Abstract).

reporting_quality.justification: A CONSORT-style framework is the closest fit for a prospective interventional trial report, and the manuscript provides core elements including patient population, treatment schema (dose and schedule), endpoint definitions, and follow-up duration (Methods; Abstract). However, because the trial is single-arm and key statistical details are deferred to the Data Supplement, reporting transparency in the normalized main text is moderate rather than complete (Methods). The normalized manuscript does not include a clear data or code sharing statement or repository identifiers, so reproducibility beyond the described protocol and supplemental materials appears limited.

novelty_literature.justification: The manuscript contributes clinically meaningful novelty by demonstrating sustained long-term benefit of adding blinatumomab to frontline therapy in infants with KMT2A-rearranged ALL, a subgroup with historically poor outcomes and limited evidence base (Abstract; Introduction). It extends prior short-term reports from the same pilot effort by providing multi-year DFS/OS, infection support measures, and pharmacokinetics in this very young population (Abstract; Methods). The design remains early-phase and historically controlled, but the magnitude and durability of the observed outcome differences represent a notable advance that motivates confirmation in ongoing trials (Discussion; Conclusions).

writing_presentation.justification: The paper is clearly structured and the abstract is quantitative, specifying cohort size, follow-up duration, survival outcomes versus historical controls, and key supportive care/toxicity and pharmacokinetic parameters (Abstract). Methods concisely describe the treatment timing relative to Interfant-06 blocks, endpoint definitions, and the nature of the historical-control comparisons (Methods). The discussion appropriately tempers interpretation by acknowledging limitations of historical comparisons and differing adverse-event classification systems, while pointing to ongoing confirmatory trials (Discussion).

key_strengths: Addresses a high-risk, rare pediatric leukemia subgroup with a clear unmet need.
Reports durable long-term DFS/OS improvements compared with selected and matched Interfant-06 historical controls.
Clinically relevant secondary outcomes including infection/supportive care use and pharmacokinetic characterization in infants.
Transparent acknowledgment that confirmatory randomized/modern trials are ongoing.
key_concerns: Single-arm design with historical controls leaves substantial risk of residual confounding and temporal/center effects.
Small sample size (n = 30) limits precision and subgroup interpretability.
Key statistical analysis details are relegated to the Data Supplement and are not fully recoverable from the normalized main text.
Data/code sharing and reproducibility artifacts are not clearly described in the normalized manuscript.
chief_reviewer.rationale: The study provides compelling early evidence of durable benefit in a very high-risk population, but the small, single-arm historically controlled design keeps it in a mid-tier clinical oncology journal band pending confirmation in ongoing trials.
